chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn Ameyra, from Abdul Al-'ala ibn Ayn, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The greatest of arrogance is belittling the people and considering the Truth as foolish.' I said: 'And what is belittling the people and considering the Truth as foolish?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Ignoring the Truth and maligning its people. So whoever does that, he has snatched from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, His Gown (of Pride).'

key_terms.رِدَاءَهُ: His Gown (referring to Allah's attribute of Pride/Majesty)
key_terms.سَفَهُ الْحَقِّ: Considering the Truth as foolish or insignificant
key_terms.يَجْهَلُ الْحَقَّ: Ignoring or treating the Truth with ignorance

ai.seo_question: What is the greatest form of arrogance according to the Prophet and Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates that true arrogance is not merely haughtiness but the active rejection of truth and disparagement of its people, a state described as competing with Allah in wearing the 'Gown of Pride' (rida al-kibr). This concept is deeply rooted in Shia exegesis, linking human hubris to the divine attribute of pride, as seen in the story of Iblis who claimed 'I am better than him' (Quran 7:12). The hadith thus elevates arrogance from a social vice to a theological rebellion against the Creator's authority.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Sayf Bin Ameyra, from Abdul Al’ala Bin Ayn who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The greatest of the arrogance is belittling the people and considering the Truth as foolish’. I said, ‘And what (constitutes) belittling the people and considering the Truth as foolish?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said, ‘Ignoring the Truth and maligning upon its people. So the one who does that, so he has snatched from Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic, His<sup>azwj</sup> Gown (of Pride)’.
en.sarwar: 9. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Sayf ibn ‘Amirah from ‘Abd al-‘Ala’ ibn ‘A’Yun who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘The Messenger of Allah has said, “The biggest form of arrogance is to sink (belittle or look down upon) people and consider the truth foolishness.” I (the narrator) then asked, ‘What is to ‘sink’ the people and hoodwink the truth?’ The Imam said, ‘It is ignoring the truth and criticizing the people of truth. Whoever does it has disputed Allah, the Majestic, the Glorious, about His gown.’””
